title: Tamil Nadu Politics – Morning Brief – 14 November 2026
headline: Tamil Nadu Imposes Strict Stock Limits on Essential Food Commodities to Curb Inflation Spike

sections.big_picture:
The political landscape of Tamil Nadu is undergoing intense turbulence as the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) administration under Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay navigates simultaneous challenges on economic, legislative, and law-and-order fronts. With the Union government reporting a state inflation rate peaking at 7.29% in October, the state government has responded by imposing stringent stock limits on paddy, rice, tur, and urad pulses to safeguard vulnerable consumers from soaring market prices.

Simultaneously, the administration faces mounting pressure from major political opponents. AIADMK General Secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami and PMK President Anbumani Ramadoss have launched scathing attacks against the Chief Minister, questioning governance efficiency, industrial project clearance claims, and safety protocols for women and children. Compounding the political friction, controversies surrounding local party functionaries have erupted, forcing senior leaders across party lines to demand immediate legal accountability and transparent internal disciplinary mechanisms.

sections.government_and_administration: - **CM Vijay Announces ₹5,000 Monthly Salary Hike for 9,646 Guest Lecturers:** Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has issued formal government orders revising the monthly honorarium for 9,646 guest faculty members working across government arts, science, education, engineering, and polytechnic colleges, effective November 1. Following this administrative revision, remuneration for lecturers in arts, science, education, and engineering colleges increases from ₹30,000 to ₹35,000 per month. The financial decision aims to address long-standing wage stagnation demands raised by higher education instructors across state-run institutions. Officials confirmed that the state exchequer will disburse the augmented salaries starting next month to ensure immediate fiscal relief for educators. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/tamil-nadu-guest-faculty-get-rs-5000-salary-hike))
sections.political_parties_and_opposition: - **BJP National Vice-President Ram Madhav Warns TVK Against Alliance with Congress:** Bharatiya Janata Party national vice-president Ram Madhav has issued a direct political warning to Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and TVK founder C. Joseph Vijay, advising him to remain highly cautious of any future political alliance with the Congress party. Speaking at a party conference, Madhav characterized Congress as an inherently untrustworthy political entity with a historical precedent of backstabbing and undermining regional coalition partners for partisan electoral gains. The warning comes amid intense speculation regarding political realignments ahead of upcoming electoral contests in the state. TVK leadership has not yet issued a formal rebuttal to the BJP leader's remarks, maintaining strategic silence as opposition parties attempt to shape the state's unfolding political narrative. ([The Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/chennai/bjp-asks-vijay-to-be-wary-of-congress/articleshow/135814100.cms))
sections.assembly_courts_and_policy: - **Madras High Court Refuses to Dismiss Election Petition Against Udhayanidhi Stalin's 2026 Victory:** The Madras High Court has dismissed two interlocutory applications filed by Leader of the Opposition and DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin, refusing to strike down an election petition challenging his victory from the Chepauk-Thiruvallikeni Assembly constituency in the 2026 general elections. Justice Arul Murugan delivered the ruling on a petition filed by P. Milany of Theni district, which alleged material false disclosures and non-compliance with statutory election affidavit norms by the petitioner. The court ruled that substantial pleadings in the petition warrant a full judicial trial rather than summary dismissal at the threshold stage. Legal counsels for the opposition leader had argued that the petition lacked requisite factual foundations under the Representation of the People Act, but the bench overruled these objections, setting the stage for formal evidentiary hearings. ([The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/madras-high-court-refuses-to-reject-election-plea-against-udhayanidhis-win-chepauk-thiruvallikeni/article71696602.ece))
sections.district_developments: - **TVK Karamadai Union Secretary Booked for Alleged Sexual Harassment and Caste Abuse in Coimbatore:** The Coimbatore district police have registered a criminal case against Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam’s (TVK) Karamadai union secretary, Karupusamy, following serious allegations of sexual harassment, criminal intimidation, and caste abuse lodged by a 29-year-old female party functionary. Alongside Karupusamy, police also booked a local party couple for actively abetting the harassment and subjecting the complainant to caste-based insults. The incident triggered massive political outrage, prompting VCK leader Thol Thirumavalavan and DMK leaders to demand immediate, uncompromising legal action against the accused office-bearer. In response to the police inaction initially alleged by local cadres, TVK women cadres staged vocal protests in Arni and locked local party offices, demanding the immediate expulsion of the accused functionary to protect party integrity. ([The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/tvk-karamadai-union-secretary-booked-on-sexual-harassment-charge/article71698486.ece))
sections.what_to_watch_next: Over the next 24 to 48 hours, political observers will closely monitor the legal fallout from the Madras High Court's refusal to dismiss the election petition against Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, as well as subsequent legal notices expected in the CB-CID probe into the Isha Yoga Centre missing person case. State political circles will focus heavily on how the TVK leadership handles internal disciplinary actions regarding the sexual harassment case lodged against its Coimbatore union secretary, which has drawn intense condemnation from allied and opposition parties alike. Additionally, civil supplies departments across all 38 districts will begin strict enforcement inspections of commercial godowns to enforce the newly implemented stock limits on paddy, rice, and pulses, with trade bodies anticipated to release formal responses regarding potential market disruptions.
